claims.text: The AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 alloy is produced by spark plasma sintering and has a multiphase microstructure.
The SPS AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 alloy has finely distributed microstructural features without appreciable coarsening during processing.
The AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 microstructure is eutectic.
At elevated temperature under atmospheric conditions, AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 forms a protective oxide layer that improves wear resistance.
Accelerated simultaneous wear and corrosion is primarily caused by cyclic breakdown and unstable reformation of oxide at eutectic phase interfaces.
Mechanical wear at elevated temperature spalls the initially protective oxide film.
Oxide spallation exposes dissimilar eutectic phases.
Potential differences between exposed dissimilar phases create localized micro-galvanic cells.
Localized micro-galvanic cells accelerate selective dissolution and localized corrosion at phase boundaries.
Rapid re-oxidation after wear produces a metastable and compositionally inhomogeneous oxide film.
Compositionally uneven oxide regions contribute to localized galvanic differences.
Localized corrosion weakens mechanical cohesion at phase interfaces and thereby increases wear.
The interaction between oxide spallation, galvanic corrosion, and interfacial weakening establishes a synergistic degradation cycle.
Pre-oxidation will produce a continuous oxide film that remains more stable during wear than the oxide on a fresh surface.
Fresh-surface specimens will exhibit approximately 50% greater total material loss than pre-oxidized specimens.
Fresh-surface specimens will show more localized corrosion at eutectic phase interfaces than pre-oxidized specimens.
Fresh-surface specimens will have higher wear rates and more frequent and severe oxide-spallation events than pre-oxidized specimens.
The comparison will hold mechanical loading and sliding speed identical while varying whether the surface is fresh or pre-oxidized.
Testing is proposed at approximately 300°C with controlled oxygen partial pressure and a chloride-containing electrolyte.
Failure to observe reduced localized corrosion and wear in the pre-oxidized group, together with failure to correlate spallation with galvanic activity, would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The setup combines an aqueous NaCl solution at approximately 300°C with atmospheric conditions. A conventional aqueous solution cannot remain liquid at 300°C at atmospheric pressure; a pressurized cell, molten salt, vapor/aerosol exposure, or a lower temperature would need to be specified.
